read_extent: All seven author pages read as extracted text. Exact government bill cover and physical pages 16–18 and 22–23 independently read. Full substantive BNetzA auction-result press releases of 12 July 2023 and 21 June 2024 read.

claim.original: durchschnittlichen Geboten von 750 Mio. € pro GW
claim.translation_en: Translation: average bids of EUR 750 million per GW.

request.description: Single-stage awards directly through two-way contracts for difference, with additional PPA flexibility.

check: The official 2023 non-centrally surveyed awards total EUR 12.6 billion for 7 GW; the corresponding 2024 awards total EUR 3.0225 billion for 2.5 GW. These nominal winning-payment figures do not reproduce EUR 750 million per GW. But they do not uniquely identify the author’s unspecified average: all bids versus winning awards, included auction cohorts, weighting and discounting are not stated.
benign_alternatives: Both official press releases explain that 90% of payment is spread over twenty annual instalments from completion. Discounted economic burden can be materially lower than the nominal award sum; capital costs and refinancing are the author’s immediate context. No unique discounted correction is asserted.
The term bids may include unsuccessful bids rather than only award payments. No underlying distribution or explicit averaging method is identified.
An indexed central-auction total is not a substitute for identifying the author’s denominator. Missing methodology is not proof of error.

draft.addressed_version: Government WindSeeG bill BT 21/8238, 28 September 2026, is the closest matching parliamentary version.
draft.exactness_limit: The author identifies the government bill and sections 20 and 54c, and the two-stage design matches this version, but does not print a Bundestag number or draft date. Exact version identity is therefore not asserted as independently proved.

secondary_screen.disposition: Not promoted. The statement about all other relevant European markets having indexed single-stage CfDs is broad, but comparison with a future German auction framework and an implicit fixed-bottom market scope gives substantive alternatives. Dutch 2026 subsidies versus planned 2027 CfDs and Norwegian floating investment aid are not treated as conclusive matched counterexamples.

limits: No actual financing burden, auction attractiveness, electricity-price effect, policy merits or author intent is established. No issue record created.
